_comment: Ground truth for F1 client-side pre-submit validation. Every message string must be BYTE-IDENTICAL to what lib/vendor-submissions.ts (server) already produces for the same violation, so the existing humaniseFieldError() mapping in lib/vendor-register-response.ts keeps working unmodified -- this is a new client-side check that reuses the server's own vocabulary, not a second vocabulary.

exportedFunction.name: validateVendorRegisterFormClientSide
exportedFunction.returns: Array of raw error message strings, same shape/vocabulary as validateVendorSubmissionInput()'s errors array. Empty array means the form is submittable.
exportedFunction.purity: Pure function of state only. No DOM access, no fetch, no side effects -- must be callable and assertable in isolation.

strictIntegerRule.description: Number.parseInt('1.5', 10) === 1 and Number.parseInt('1e3', 10) === 1 -- both silently accept malformed input as valid integers. The client validator must NOT use Number.parseInt to decide validity. Use a strict whole-number regex against the raw string instead.
strictIntegerRule.onBlankOptionalField: tableCount/chairCount/staffPerDay are optional -- an empty string is NOT a violation for these three. Only validate format when the string is non-empty.
strictIntegerRule.onBlankBoothCount: boothCount is required -- an empty string IS a violation (falls through to the 'is required' message below).

checks.message: businessName is required and must be a non-empty string
contactPersonName is required and must be a non-empty string
contactCellPhone is required and must be a non-empty string
contactEmail is required and must be a non-empty string
productDescription is required and must be a non-empty string
vendorCategory is required and must be a non-empty array
checks.note: Fixes the P2 backlog item: vendorCategory fieldset claims aria-required but nothing enforced it. This is now the enforcement.

checks.message: boothCount is required and must be a positive integer
checks.note: This is the root-cause fix for Brad's 'submit did nothing' report. '1.5', '1e3', 'e1', '', '0', '-1' must ALL fail this check and produce this exact message -- none may silently become NaN/null/1.

checks.message: tableCount must be a non-negative integer
chairCount must be a non-negative integer
staffPerDay must be a non-negative integer
powerRequired is required and must be a boolean

wiring.description: VendorRegisterForm.tsx's handleSubmit must call validateVendorRegisterFormClientSide(state) BEFORE the fetch() call. If the returned array is non-empty: set descriptor to { kind: 'validation-error', message: 'Please check the highlighted fields.', fieldErrors: <the array> } via the EXISTING setDescriptor/setStatus('error') path, and return WITHOUT calling fetch. Do not add a second banner component or a second scroll/focus mechanism -- the existing bannerRef useEffect (VendorRegisterForm.tsx lines ~68-74) already scrolls/focuses on any non-success descriptor change, and humaniseFieldError already turns each raw message into copy. Reuse both unchanged.
wiring.mustNotFetch: A network request (fetch to /api/vendors/register) must NOT be observed when validateVendorRegisterFormClientSide returns a non-empty array.

conditionalFields._comment: Verified directly against source 2026-08-18 by @architect -- the backlog's claim that the food fields already gate correctly on category was WRONG. As of components/vendors/VendorCategoryFieldset.tsx and VendorBoothFieldset.tsx today, NONE of the three fields below have any conditional render or payload exclusion. All three share one bug, fixed with two shared guard functions.

guardFunctions.isElectricalLoadApplicable: export function isElectricalLoadApplicable(state: VendorRegisterFormState): boolean { return state.powerRequired === 'true'; }
guardFunctions.isFoodRetailer: export function isFoodRetailer(state: VendorRegisterFormState): boolean { return state.vendorCategory.includes('food-retailer'); }

fields.renderRule: Only render the VendorFormField for electricalLoad when isElectricalLoadApplicable(state) is true. Use a JSX ternary: {isElectricalLoadApplicable(state) ? (<VendorFormField fieldKey="electricalLoad" .../>) : null}

placeholders._comment: VendorFormField currently has no placeholder prop at all. Add one optional prop, threaded to both the <input> and <textarea> branches. Placeholders are format/example hints only -- never a prefilled default value in form state (a prefilled value could be silently submitted if the user never touches the field; a placeholder cannot, since it is never part of `value`).
placeholders.propAddition: placeholder?: string on VendorFormFieldProps, passed to both <input placeholder={placeholder}> and <textarea placeholder={placeholder}>
